verdict.rationale: cubic documents an Analytics API for exporting pull-request analytics via API key, with a machine-readable OpenAPI spec. Its review configuration and custom agents live in a repo-hosted cubic.yaml file, so they stay in the user's own repository. However, no documented full-account data export or offboarding path exists, and the analytics export is gated to Pro/Max. missing for 10: a documented export of all account data (learned memories, wiki, scan findings, review history), a stated open export format for a bulk takeout, an account deletion/offboarding procedure, availability outside Pro/Max, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Export pull request analytics with a personal or organization API key. Access requires Pro or Max.
The Analytics API gives you PR-level data on how many issues were flagged, how many were fixed, how much AI code was authored, etc.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
